collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — PONDERING HOW LIFE HAS GONE (LIF-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Adults of every age looking at their own lives so far: roads not taken, quiet satisfaction, small regrets, unexpected pride, things left unfinished, luck, gratitude and plenty of amusement. Nobody has to reach a verdict.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult aged 30 or older)

collection.description: A villager suddenly remembers an unkind remark from years ago: go and say sorry, or be kinder today instead.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Out of nowhere, while weeding, (name1) remembers something unkind (he/she) said to somebody years ago. It wasn't terrible. It was a sharp little remark, said to be clever. (He/she) remembers the person's face changing. (He/she) hadn't thought about it in years. Now (he/she) can't stop thinking about it.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (name1) doesn't know if the person would even remember, or want to be reminded. So (he/she) just goes through the rest of the day more carefully, watching what (he/she) says. It's harder than (he/she) expected. At one point (he/she) opens (his/her) mouth to say something sharp and clever, and closes it again. (He/she) thinks that might be the closest thing to sorry (he/she) can manage today.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: The person still lives in the village, and (name1) goes and finds them. It's awkward. They don't even remember it at first. Then they do. "Oh. That." They're quiet for a moment. "Thank you for saying so." That's all. It doesn't fix anything that happened back then. (name1) walks home feeling lighter anyway, and a little foolish, and glad.
